title: One Trajectory, Two Requirements: Accuracy and Local Stability in Euler Sampling for Flow Matching Policies
abstract: arXiv:2611.13311v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Flow matching robot policies commonly use a fixed Euler step count selected from offline accuracy sweeps. At inference time, however, each policy input (visual observation, robot state, and language instruction) together with a source-noise draw defines a different ODE trajectory and sequence of local Jacobians. We ask whether a step count that accurately follows the nominal noise-to-action trajectory can still be too coarse for strongly contracting directions around it. An exact two-coordinate system and a controlled augmentation of six trained flow models show that trajectory accuracy and local Euler stability can impose different step requirements even when the original learned transport is unchanged. We then study a frozen $\pi_{0.5}$-LIBERO checkpoint without modifying its weights or action dynamics. translated_title: 一条轨迹，两种需求：流匹配策略欧拉采样中的精度与局部稳定性
translated_abstract: 流匹配机器人策略通常使用由离线精度扫描选定的固定欧拉步数。然而在推理时，每个策略输入（视觉观测、机器人状态和语言指令）连同一次源噪声采样，共同定义了一条不同的常微分方程（ODE）轨迹以及局部雅可比矩阵序列。我们由此提出问题：能够精确跟随名义上“噪声到动作”轨迹的步数，对于其周围强烈收缩的方向而言是否仍然过于粗糙。一个精确的双坐标系系统以及对六个已训练流模型的受控扩展实验表明，即使原始学习到的输运过程保持不变，轨迹精度与局部欧拉稳定性也可能施加不同的步数要求。随后，我们在不修改权重或动作动力学的前提下，研究了一个冻结的 π0.5-LIBERO 检查点。在来自 10 个 LIBERO-10 任务的 30 个策略输入上，雅可比矩阵在动作端点附近表现出强烈的收缩方向，然而……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文通过精确双坐标系实验证明，流匹配策略的欧拉采样中轨迹精度与局部稳定性对步数的要求可能不一致，并在冻结的 π0.5-LIBERO 策略中发现动作端点附近存在强收缩方向。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that trajectory accuracy and local Euler stability can impose different step requirements in flow matching policies, revealing strong contracting directions near the action endpoint of a frozen π0.5-LIBERO checkpoint.
